clue.text: One making predictions of advantage to those who listen

indicators.note: the phrase asks for what a listener hears, so the word for gain is taken by its sound

parts.note: something of advantage brings profit, a gain

explanation.surface: A forecaster whose forecasts pay off for anyone who pays attention.
explanation.definitionFit: A seer or oracle foretells the future, the classic maker of predictions.

clue.text: Fasten up aged hounds outside

indicators.note: outside means the hounds go around the other piece

parts.note: a pack is a group of hounds

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom, so the word for aged is reversed

parts.note: aged means old

explanation.surface: Shutting in elderly dogs from the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' is the reversal signal, natural in a down clue; 'hounds' is a noun here, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A padlock is a detachable lock, and to padlock a gate is to secure it shut.

clue.text: They are lacking round embassies

parts.note: O is round in shape
missions are diplomatic embassies

explanation.surface: Diplomats short of something in their circuit of foreign posts.
explanation.definitionFit: Things left out or neglected are gaps, the items that are lacking.

clue.text: It could turn a girl's head

definitions.text: It could turn a girl's head

parts.words: It could turn a girl's head
parts.note: not flattery that dazzles her but a reddish dye that changes the colour of her hair

explanation.surface: Something that might make a young woman fall for someone.
explanation.definitionFit: This reddish-brown plant dye is used to colour hair.

clue.text: Skinny and toothless what's-his-name

parts.note: skinny means thin
a toothless mouth shows only gums, so it is gummy

explanation.surface: A thin, toothless old man whose name escapes us.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial placeholder used for a person or thing whose name is forgotten.

clue.text: Relative with a name for being lewd

parts.note: an uncle is a family relative

explanation.surface: A family member notorious for smutty behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclean in the moral sense means impure or indecent, as lewd talk is.

clue.text: 7 transposed and distressed

indicators.note: transposed means the two parts of the phrase change places

parts.note: 7 down is ERECT, which means set up

explanation.surface: A number that has been moved and is upset about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 down's answer, ERECT, means SET UP; swapping its two halves gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being upset means feeling troubled or agitated.

clue.text: Copper has communist girl up for removing water in the kitchen

definitions.text: for removing water in the kitchen

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: red is a common label for a communist
Nell is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A policeman has a left-wing girlfriend who drains things in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman; it is the metal, CU. 'up' reverses RED + NELL to LLENDER. The answer is an old spelling of colander.
explanation.definitionFit: A perforated bowl for draining vegetables, an old spelling of colander.

clue.text: Not inclined to raise

explanation.surface: Someone reluctant to lift something.
explanation.definitionFit: Upright means not leaning at an angle; and to build or put up is the verb sense.

clue.text: After making deductions, was first to be stung

parts.note: nett (net) is the amount left after deductions
led means was in front, was first

explanation.surface: Someone who was first in line to be stung after deductions from pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Nettled means irritated or annoyed, as if by a stinging plant.

clue.text: Hamlet, perhaps, said to be condescending

indicators.note: said tells us to take the word as it is spoken, not as written

parts.note: Hamlet was Prince of Denmark, so he is an example of a Dane

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's prince is reputed to look down on others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamlet' seems to be the play or a small village; here he is the Danish prince, a DANE, and that word spoken gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to stoop to do something, acting as if it is beneath one's dignity.

clue.text: Broke victor's head — rude about it

indicators.note: about means the word for rude goes round the other piece, with it pointing back to the victor's head

parts.note: insolent means rude, disrespectful

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of victor

explanation.surface: A winner's leader is disrespectful, and the winner is penniless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers back to the victor's head, the V that INSOLENT goes about.
explanation.definitionFit: Being broke means having no money, unable to pay debts, the state of bankruptcy.

clue.text: Attack somebody unendingly, killing without hesitation

indicators.note: unendingly means the word for somebody loses its final letter

parts.note: one means somebody, as in 'one should know'

indicators.note: without tells us the hesitation sound is removed from the word for killing

parts.note: slaughter is killing on a large scale
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A violent assault on someone, carried out without a pause, ending in a killing.
explanation.definitionFit: An onslaught is a fierce assault or charge.

clue.text: Crack up former spouse looking, back, one whose wife did that

parts.note: an ex is a former husband or wife

indicators.note: the clue's looking back tells us to read the biblical name backwards

parts.note: in Genesis Lot's wife looked back at Sodom and was turned to a pillar of salt

explanation.surface: A divorcee glancing over their shoulder, like the biblical woman who turned to salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack up' is not breaking down but its other sense, to praise highly. 'looking back' does double duty in the surface: Lot's wife looked back, and 'back' reverses LOT to give TOL.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack something up is to praise it extravagantly, to laud it.

clue.text: Hit head back, semi-stun

indicators.note: back tells us to read the slang word for head backwards

parts.note: conk is slang for the head (or nose)

indicators.note: semi- means only half of the word for stun is used

parts.note: KO, a knockout, stuns an opponent

explanation.surface: A blow to the skull sends someone back, half-dazed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns CONK into KNOC; 'semi-' keeps half of KO, the K.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock is to strike or rap something with a blow.

clue.text: Border flag

parts.note: a kerb is the raised border of a road or pavement
a flag is a flat paving stone

explanation.surface: A banner flown at a frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' looks like a banner but is a flagstone, a slab; the whole clue also describes the answer, a slab edging the pavement.
explanation.definitionFit: The edging slabs along a pavement form its raised border, each one a stone.

clue.text: Wound about arm needed to be treated

indicators.note: treated means the letters are processed and worked into a new order

explanation.surface: An injured arm requires medical care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' looks like an injury, matching the arm; it is the past tense of wind, so 'Wound about' means wandered.
explanation.definitionFit: A path or river that wound about twisted and turned in loops.

clue.text: Bill and Bob at one about being nimble

parts.note: AC, account, is a bill
printed as Bob, but the wordplay needs the name Rob
I is the Roman numeral one
C, circa, means about

explanation.surface: Two men united in being agile.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints Bob, but the letters need Rob: AC + ROB + AT + I + C. 'at one' is not unity but AT and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrobatic means agile and gymnastic, like a circus tumbler.

clue.text: An interpretation — finish it in wrought iron

indicators.note: in means the pieces go inside the worked metal
wrought means worked or shaped, so the letters of iron are rearranged

parts.note: end means finish

explanation.surface: A suggested reading: complete the piece in ornamental metalwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrought iron' looks like the metal itself; 'wrought' is the anagram signal working on 'iron'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rendition is a performance or version of a piece, someone's reading of it.

clue.text: It could be HMS Siva

parts.note: HMS marks a Royal Navy warship, and Siva is the Hindu god known as the ..., so a warship named after him fits a type of fighting ship

explanation.surface: A naval vessel named after a Hindu deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiva's role in the Hindu trinity is to annihilate, and a fast naval escort ship has the same name.

clue.text: Edward, inwardly simple, brought up to be bold

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means read from bottom to top
inwardly means the word for simple goes inside the name

parts.note: Ted is a short form of Edward
naif means simple, naive

explanation.surface: Edward, simple at heart, was raised to be brave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inwardly' is the container signal and 'brought up' reverses the whole result, apt in a down clue. NAIF is the French-derived spelling of naive.
explanation.definitionFit: Being defiant means openly resisting, daring and unafraid.

clue.text: Compass point in vogue

indicators.note: in means the compass point goes inside the word for vogue

parts.note: a rage is a craze, something in vogue
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A direction on the dial that happens to be fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compass point' reads as one phrase; split it, 'Compass' as scope or extent is the definition and 'point' is N.
explanation.definitionFit: Compass in the sense of scope or extent means the reach covered by something.

clue.text: Quarters he can put in order and improve

parts.note: E and N, east and north, are quarters of the compass

indicators.note: put in order means the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Rooms someone can tidy and make better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarters' looks like lodgings; it is two compass points, E and N.
explanation.definitionFit: To enhance is to make better or increase in quality.

clue.text: Tries to escape a part in the theatre

explanation.surface: An actor trying to run away from a role.
explanation.definitionFit: One who flees takes flight; and the space above a stage where scenery is hung is called by the same name.

clue.text: Climber holds gold key

indicators.note: holds means the climbing plant contains the other piece

parts.note: ivy is a climbing plant
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A mountaineer clutching a golden key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' looks like a mountaineer; it is the plant. Piano keys were traditionally made of this material.
explanation.definitionFit: Piano keys were faced with elephant tusk, so the word is slang for a key.

clue.text: Some shillings to wager, say — it goes on runners

parts.note: a bob was slang for a shilling, an old British coin, so some are bobs

indicators.note: say asks for the word as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: to lay is to wager, as in lay a bet

explanation.surface: Betting a few shillings, on a horse with runners at a race meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runners' suggests horses at a race; here they are the blades a sled glides on.
explanation.definitionFit: A sled for racing down ice tracks glides on steel runners.

clue.text: Concise instructions

explanation.surface: A short set of directions.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief means short and to the point; and a lawyer's or agent's set of directions is also called one.

clue.text: Proverbially happy lamb

explanation.surface: A lamb that is famously cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happy as Larry' is a British saying for very contented; Larry the Lamb was a puppet in the old BBC radio Toytown stories.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'happy as Larry' means very content; Larry the Lamb was a children's radio character.

clue.text: The defender has a game point

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
the gist is the main point

explanation.surface: A footballer at the back has a scoring chance.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who argues in defence of a belief or cause is an apologist.

clue.text: Aural drops prevail

indicators.note: aural refers to hearing, so the word for drops is taken as it sounds

parts.note: rain falls in drops

explanation.surface: Ear drops win the day.
explanation.definitionFit: To reign is to rule or hold sway, to predominate.

clue.text: Reflexively, you see the fly's swatted

indicators.note: a swatted fly is squashed and broken up, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: You watch the insect get flattened by a quick reflex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflexively' suggests a quick reaction; it means the reflexive pronoun, the archaic form of yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic reflexive pronoun for the second person singular, as in 'know yourself' in old English.

clue.text: Start spelling 13 phonetically — hot stuff!

indicators.note: phonetically means the letters are said as their names, kay and en

parts.note: 13 across is KNOCK, and the start of spelling it out is K, N

explanation.surface: An instruction to begin saying a word letter by letter, followed by a cry about spicy food.
explanation.walkthrough: Spelling 13 across aloud starts 'kay, en', which runs together as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This fiery red pepper powder is a spice that burns the mouth.
